query: What experiences do iPhone 11 buyers report when using SIM cards with different carriers?

chunks.text: Perfect cosmetically but buyer beware. This phone was suppose to be unlocked to any carrier. My airtalk wireless sims card would not work in it. I ended up have to get an H20 (knockoff AT&T) phone plan and sims card. Which mean I had to change my number and was a head ache all the way around. But it works fine now and seems to have decent battery life so that’s a plus.
chunks.scoring_query: What experiences do buyers report when using SIM cards with different carriers?

chunks.text: As for the functionality of the phone, it works great. My sim card runs on GSM, so I needed an IMEI phone, and the description on amazon said it supported GSM sim card carriers, so that’s one of the reasons I made this purchase. I was able to make calls, texts, and use my cellular data immediately once I was done setting up the phone. As a side note, this phone actually runs with IMEI and MEID, so any sim card carrier would’ve worked with it, which comforting to know. The sound also works great. I was worried about this, especially, because I was reading the negative reviews, and they were saying the earbuds sound was hollow, but for me, it wasn’t that way.
chunks.scoring_query: What experiences do buyers report when using SIM cards with different carriers?

chunks.text: Recommend! Was in Mint condition. I had some thought and did some research buying a refurbished phone. The phone itself came in mint condition! No cracks or scratches. Works smoothly with no issues, good battery life. Just to verify! if you get an unlocked phone and have a hard time wonder why your SIM card is going through but says “no service”... before you get paranoid... (go to the settings... select general... Select about... then scroll till you see carrier lock... it should say (NO SIM RESTRICTIONS)... that’s how you know it’s unlocked to any carrier. If your SIM does go through but it read’s it with no service you have to go to your carrier and have them switch the SIM card on to your new phone from your old device. You’re welcome! I very recommend, do your research before purchasing. Enjoy your day

chunks.text: Buyer beware. Buyer beware... be very careful buying these refurbished phones. I received mine which was supposed to be able to be used on T-Mobile's network. I took it into the store to link it to my plan and was informed that it could not be used because it is currently registered to another user. So it either was not wiped clean or was stolen. Returned and received a refund.

chunks.text: Sent phone for wrong carrier. Product received today on time, in the correct memory size and color, and in excellent shape. However, upon inserting the SIM card and trying to set it up, I learned that it is carrier-locked to Boost Mobile. I had ordered a phone compatible with T-Mobile. Hopefully Boost can unlock it tomorrow but now I have to wait another day when I should have just been able to swap in my existing SIM card and be ready to go. I would recommend ordering unlocked for nearly the same price, not worth the hassle trying to fix this.
